description: The order uses a token that is not in the IPS universe. Default is deny.
The order targets a protocol that is not in the IPS universe.
The order calls a function that is not in the IPS universe.
The order's recipient is not in the IPS universe.
An approve order asks for an unlimited or larger-than-needed allowance. Only the exact amount may be approved.
The order value is above the per-transaction limit.
The order would push the 24-hour spend above the daily limit.
The order would exceed the maximum number of transactions per hour.
After the order, one asset would be above its maximum portfolio weight.
After the order, the stablecoin weight would be below the minimum.
The portfolio is inside the rebalance band, so nothing is done. This is a no-action reason, not a violation.
The pool TVL is below the IPS minimum.
Too much of the yield comes from reward tokens.
The current APY deviates from its 30-day mean by more than the IPS allows.
A stablecoin involved is further from 1 USD than the IPS allows.
The lending pool utilization is above the IPS maximum.
The simulated or requested slippage is above the IPS maximum.
The estimated benefit is below the required multiple of the estimated cost.
A risk input is older than the IPS maximum age or is missing.
The tier is T0, so the agent may not place orders.
The tier is T1: the order is a proposal only and is never sent by the agent. Reserved; no v1 code path uses T1.
The emergency stop is engaged. Orders are denied while it is engaged and the engaging record uses this code. It is a status, not a violation.
The owner released the emergency stop. It is a status, not a violation.
The order is above the approval threshold and waits for the owner. This is the T3 behaviour; it is a rule, not a tier.
The owner rejected a pending order.
